newsitem.title: CANADA: Hydro-Quebec seeks to divert rivers - report.
newsitem.headline: Hydro-Quebec seeks to divert rivers - report.

text.p: Hydro-Quebec, facing lower than normal water levels in some of its reservoirs, has asked the provincial government for permission to divert some rivers in northern Quebec, Montreal daily newspaper Le Devoir reported on Wednesday.
Citing documents obtained under access to information provisions, Le Devoir said Hydro-Quebec Chief Executive Andre Caille filed the request on March 14.
Hydro-Quebec asked permission to divert rivers in the North Shore and Lac-Saint-Jean region to help feed its Bersimis and Outardes generating stations near the Manicouagan River, Le Devoir said.
Hydro-Quebec officials could not be reached for comment on the report, but two Quebec cabinet ministers indicated that it was mainly accurate.
Natural Resources Minister Guy Chevrette told reporters that Hydro-Quebec was seeking to divert four rivers, not six as indicated in the Le Devoir report.
"There will be public hearings and there is no question of the Quebec government authorizing these projects without public hearings," Quebec Environment Minister David Cliche told Reuters.

Le Devoir said Hydro-Quebec requested permission to divert the Portneuf, Sault-aux-Cochons and Manouane Rivers toward the Bersimis 1 et 2 generating stations. It also asked to be allowed to divert the Boucher River toward its Outardes generating complex.

The newspaper said the Hydro-Quebec documents showed that the Quebec government-owned utility was facing a serious drop in water levels in its reservoirs just as it was intensifying its search for new customers in the United States.
Le Devoir said water levels in Hydro-Quebec's reservoirs were 21 percent below normal at May 1.
Hydro-Quebec generates, distributes and markets most of the electricty produced in Quebec, and exports some output to clients in the northeastern United States.
